details:
Lightning Flora – Project Details

Lightning Flora is an environmental monitoring and analysis platform designed to support sustainable agriculture and help users better understand environmental conditions.

The project brings together environmental and satellite-based data, including temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure, wind speed, vegetation health (NDVI), and soil moisture. It processes and visualizes these parameters to provide meaningful insights into environmental changes, plant health, and potential risks such as drought.

The platform includes several features: real-time-style data visualization, trend analysis, risk and alarm indicators, location comparison, an extensive environmental data dashboard, and a 3D Digital Twin that helps users explore environmental conditions in a more interactive way. It also includes hydrological and flood-related analysis features.

One of the project's key innovations is its connection between software and physical hardware. Using an Arduino UNO and an I2C LCD display, Lightning Flora can transfer selected environmental information from the computer to a physical display. Users can navigate through six different information screens using a potentiometer.

The project was developed using Python and Streamlit for the main application, Arduino C++ for hardware communication, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for interactive web features. GitHub was used for code management and development.

Lightning Flora aims to make complex environmental information accessible, understandable, and useful. By combining data analysis, interactive visualization, and physical hardware, the project offers an innovative approach to environmental awareness and sustainable agriculture. Its long-term goal is to help users make more informed decisions, protect vegetation, and contribute to a more sustainable future.
